avoid_supplements.name: Sympathomimetic herbs (Ephedra, Ma Huang)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Additive sympathomimetic effects causing severe hypertension, tachycardia, and arrhythmias
avoid_supplements.action: Contraindicated; counsel patient to avoid completely

avoid_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
avoid_supplements.mechanism: MAO inhibition properties may potentiate epinephrine effects and increase risk of hypertensive crisis
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; consider alternative antidepressant if epinephrine needed chronically

avoid_supplements.name: Tyramine-containing supplements
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Risk of hypertensive crisis when combined with epinephrine, especially in anaphylaxis settings
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid high-dose supplements; limit dietary tyramine intake

caution_supplements.name: Caffeine
caution_supplements.mechanism: Mild additive stimulant effects may increase heart rate and anxiety
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for increased nervousness or palpitations; use in moderation

caution_supplements.name: Ginseng
caution_supplements.mechanism: Weak sympathomimetic properties may enhance epinephrine effects
caution_supplements.action: Monitor vital signs; use moderate doses only

avoid_foods.name: Aged cheeses, cured meats, fermented foods (high tyramine)
avoid_foods.mechanism: Tyramine interaction may precipitate hypertensive crisis, particularly concerning during epinephrine emergency use
avoid_foods.action: Counsel patient to limit tyramine intake; especially important if on concurrent MAO inhibitors

caution_foods.name: Caffeine-containing foods (chocolate, coffee, tea)
caution_foods.mechanism: Additive sympathomimetic effects may increase heart rate and tremor
caution_foods.action: Monitor tolerance; counsel moderation, especially in anxiety-prone patients

monitoring_notes: Monitor blood pressure, heart rate, and cardiac rhythm, particularly when epinephrine is used for emergency conditions or in patients with cardiovascular disease. Assess for additive sympathomimetic effects if patient uses stimulant-containing supplements or foods.
